whoIsMtf.heading: WHO IS MTF?
lines: MTF brings together the public sector, private sector, academia and the next generation around one purpose:
Advancing peace, prosperity and a better quality of life through tourism.
Tourism is more than an industry. It shapes our economies, communities, cities, environment, employment, culture and quality of life.

tagline.value: THINK TOGETHER • LEARN TOGETHER • ACT TOGETHER

theme.heading: Why Mediterranean SUN?
lines: For thousands of years, the Sun has shaped Mediterranean civilisation, architecture, agriculture, food, culture and way of life.
Today, SUN represents the tourism model we want to build.
It asks three questions:

pillars.name: Stewardship
pillars.question: WHAT MUST WE PROTECT?
lines: Tourism brings opportunity — but also responsibility.
Visitors, businesses, authorities and communities all have a role in protecting the places we share.
Enjoy the destination. Respect the place.
Growth must improve the places people visit — not consume what makes them special.
pillars.closingLine: PROTECT WHAT MAKES THE MEDITERRANEAN SPECIAL.
pillars.mythMotif: Helios' cattle — 'Do not touch what belongs to the Sun.'

pillars.name: Unity
pillars.question: WHAT CAN WE ACHIEVE TOGETHER?
pillars.lead: The Mediterranean becomes stronger when it is better connected.
lines: CONNECT PEOPLE • CONNECT DESTINATIONS • CONNECT OPPORTUNITY
ACHIEVE TOGETHER WHAT WE CANNOT ACHIEVE ALONE
pillars.mythMotif: The star — the sailors who read the heavens; 'a hand when we needed one.'

pillars.name: Net Positive
pillars.question: WHAT SHOULD TOURISM LEAVE BEHIND?
lines: Tourism's success should not be measured only by arrivals, nights and expenditure.
The ultimate measure:
DOES TOURISM IMPROVE THE STANDARD OF LIVING OF THE COMMUNITIES THAT HOST IT?
Net Positive means:

gala.title: Calypso's Odyssey
gala.subtitle: The Greatest Journeys Are Not Always Across the Sea
gala.subtitleCaps: THE GREATEST JOURNEYS ARE NOT ALWAYS ACROSS THE SEA

format.structure: Preamble + seven Cantos + Conclusion; nine songs; aerial and acrobatic company; three screens
format.note: Per the 'shorter version' working script. Final production values tbc.

gala.storyline: Ulysses — King of Ithaca, husband of Penelope, father of Telemachus, the man who conquered Troy — has survived the Cyclops, Circe and the Sirens when his companions do the one thing they were warned against: they touch what belongs to the Sun, the cattle of Helios. Zeus answers with thunder; the ship breaks apart and every sailor is lost. Alone between sea and sky, with the gods silent, Ulysses does what Mediterranean sailors have always done when they lose sight of land: he reads the heavens. One star grows brighter, follows him for nine nights and, on the tenth dawn, touches the earth as the nymph Calypso on the island of Ogygia — a primeval name the story roots in Gozo: red earth at Ramla, honey-coloured limestone, caves watching the horizon, and above the bay a cave that still carries her name. Her name holds the key — kalyptein, to draw a veil. She asks the stranger his name and he answers 'Nobody'; she does not silence his grief for his brothers in arms, she simply stays beside him. Before she loves him, she saves him: one wave, one breath, one morning at a time. Mercy becomes tenderness, tenderness becomes love, and then there is paradise — thyme on the wind, olive leaves turning silver, salt, wine, music — and a woman saying 'Stay today.' Under her veil, time passes unnoticed; seven years feel like one season. Happiness brings its shadow, fear, and Calypso does what frightened hearts have always done: she tries to bargain with goodbye, offering him immortality — forever young, forever together — not to defeat death but to defeat departure. Ulysses understands what eternity had hidden from her: life matters because it ends. One night the stars — Orion, the Bear — remind him who he is; navigation awakens memory, memory awakens identity: 'I am Ulysses.' The veil tears. Calypso, knowing he will leave and afraid she is not enough, meets jealousy — but he is not returning to Penelope so much as to himself. Hermes descends with Zeus's command to release him; Olympus can command her hand but not her heart. She rebuilds his raft from the wreckage that first threw him onto her shore, and then comes the net she had woven for seven years to keep him. She cuts it. Love is not the hand that closes; love is the hand that opens. The star that once guided him toward her now guides him away. He goes home, becomes husband, father and king again — but never again the man who left — grows old beneath an olive tree, and dies; three thousand years later we still know his name. Everything disappears and the Storyteller removes his cloak: 'I am Homer.' This was never an ancient story. Calypso is each one of us — when someone enters our life and changes it, when we hold too tightly, and when life finally teaches us to open our hand. Ulysses crossed the Mediterranean; Calypso never left Ogygia. Which travelled farther? He crossed seas. She crossed herself — from loneliness to love, from love to fear, from fear to jealousy, from jealousy to loss, and from loss to freedom. She turns from the horizon and walks back toward her island, toward herself, toward life, as the Mediterranean sunrise spreads across the sea. I lived.

keyLines.text: LOVE IS NOT THE HAND THAT CLOSES.
keyLines.sentenceCase: Love is not the hand that closes.

keyLines.text: LOVE IS THE HAND THAT OPENS.
keyLines.sentenceCase: Love is the hand that opens.

keyLines.text: The Greatest Journeys Are Not Always Across the Sea
Do not touch what belongs to the Sun.
When they lost sight of earth... they read the heavens.
Where do I go from here?
A sky full of stars.
The heart of the Mediterranean. Its eye upon the sea. Its soul carved in stone. A diamond set in blue.
Kalyptein. To cover. To conceal. To draw a veil.
Sometimes courage is simply... getting up again.
I was different because you were there.
Stay today.
We rarely recognise paradise while we are living inside it.
She did not stop time. She made time... unnoticed.
And we all have our Ogygia.
Life matters because it ends.
A mortal counts life in years. An immortal counts departures.
I AM ULYSSES.
The wind may belong to destiny. The hand upon the rudder remains ours.
Perhaps that is what we must do with our own wreckage. Build from it.
Holding tighter does not stop departure. Sometimes... it turns love into a chain.
We cannot always choose what leaves us. But we can choose what the leaving makes of us.
Not every star is our destination. Some illuminate only part of our voyage.
I am Homer.
Calypso is each one of us.
He crossed seas. She crossed herself.
Perhaps immortality was never about refusing to die. Perhaps it is what remains because we lived.
I LIVED.

chapters.label: Preamble
chapters.title: The Last Ship
beats: The cattle of Helios — the Sun fills the screens.
Zeus answers; the ship breaks apart.
Ulysses alone between sea and sky; the gods answer with silence.

chapters.label: Canto I
chapters.title: The Stranger
beats: The star descends and becomes Calypso.
Ogygia — Gozo emerges: Ramla, limestone, caves, the cave that carries her name.
'Nobody.' The drowned sailors; grief; she remains beside him.

chapters.label: Canto II
chapters.title: The Awakening
beats: She saves him before she loves him.
One wave. One breath. One morning.

chapters.label: Canto III
chapters.title: Paradise
beats: Paradise has a landscape: Ramla, red earth, thyme, olive, salt, wine, music.

chapters.label: Canto IV
chapters.title: Seven Years
beats: The veil crosses the screens: time made unnoticed.

chapters.label: Canto VII
chapters.title: The Open Hand
beats: The raft built from the wreckage.
The star that guides him away.

chapters.label: Conclusion
chapters.title: The Poet
beats: Ulysses goes home; the olive tree; a leaf falls.
Three thousand years later, you know his name.
Homer's revelation: Calypso is each one of us.

songs.title: A Sky Full of Stars
songs.staging: Aerial constellations. Nine nights. One star follows Ulysses and gradually descends.

songs.title: Brothers in Arms
songs.staging: Dark straps. The drowned sailors disappear one by one.

songs.title: Caruso
songs.staging: Restrained staging. Singer and one subtle aerial duet.

songs.title: La Isla Bonita
songs.staging: The major Gozo/Ogygia spectacle: aerial hoops, ribbons, dance, sea and fire.

songs.title: Nothing Else Matters
songs.staging: Symphonic Mediterranean treatment. Two aerial straps performers move from independence toward dependency.

songs.title: Forever and Ever
songs.staging: The world ages around two unchanged figures. Eternity gradually becomes loneliness.

songs.title: The Winner Takes It All
songs.staging: Minimal beginning. Calypso alone. The emotional peak builds around her.

songs.title: I Will Survive
songs.staging: Start as a lament, not disco. Gradually grow into strength. Calypso moves from the edge of the stage to its centre.

songs.title: I Lived
songs.staging: Finale, full company, ~4:00. Michela begins alone; the whole journey returns across three screens; the aerial company rises, releases and flies; every singer returns for the climax. Calypso turns from the horizon and walks back toward Gozo. Sunrise.

seo.note: Facts inside are confirmed; the phrasing is the editor's. Venue in jsonLd must be replaced when confirmed.

voice.summary: The deck already speaks in the register pear.no is built for: one idea per line, declared not described, closed with a single capitalised line. The site's job is to keep that register and let the myth carry the transitions.

rules.why: Every deck slide and every script beat is a single-clause line. pear.no sets copy the same way — short declaratives, one thought, then air.
rules.do: Tourism brings opportunity — but also responsibility.
rules.dont: Tourism brings tremendous opportunity to the region, but it also brings with it significant responsibilities that all of us must share.

rules.why: The deck's headlines are statements, not summaries: LEAVE MORE THAN WE TAKE. / BEAUTY CREATES VALUE.
rules.dont: This session will explore how beauty can create value for destinations.

rules.rule: Every section ends on one capitalised line, like a slide.
rules.why: Each deck slide closes on a caps line (PROTECT WHAT MAKES THE MEDITERRANEAN SPECIAL.). Keep it — it is the brand's cadence. Body copy stays sentence case.
rules.do:
…and greater resident pride.

BEAUTY → QUALITY → INVESTMENT → VALUE
rules.dont: Ending a section on a paragraph or a CTA button.

rules.rule: Arrows mean progress. Bullets mean a set. Never mix them.
rules.why: The deck uses → for sequence (THINK → CHALLENGE → DESIGN → ACT) and • for lists (Protect • Respect • Preserve • Enhance).
rules.dont: Share, prepare, standardise, certify and improve.

rules.rule: Ask the real question, then answer it.
rules.why: Why SUN? asks three questions. Why now? retires one question and poses a better one. The site should think out loud the same way.
rules.do: The question is no longer: how many tourists can we attract?
rules.dont: Rhetorical questions with no answer, or questions used as headings for decoration.

rules.rule: Use the pivot: not X — Y.
rules.why: The deck's and the script's strongest lines turn on a contrast: 'not consume what makes them special'; 'AI should not simply automate… It should help us redesign'; 'Not every star is our destination.'
rules.do: AI in the back office. Humans at the front.
rules.dont: AI will improve both back-office and front-of-house operations.

rules.why: 1,600+. 31+. 60 / 40. 11. The deck never rounds up with adjectives.
rules.dont: Well over a thousand delegates from dozens of countries.

rules.rule: Concrete Mediterranean nouns over abstract ones.
rules.why: The script names the place: red earth at Ramla, honey-coloured limestone, thyme on the wind, olive leaves turning silver, salt, wine. The deck names sectors: marinas, ports, beaches, airports. Name the thing.
rules.dont: A holistic ecosystem of maritime lifestyle experiences.

rules.rule: We is the region. You appears only at the call to action — and at the revelation.
rules.why: The deck speaks as 'we' (what we protect, what we leave behind). The script withholds 'you' until Homer turns to the audience. Copy the discipline.
rules.dont: You'll discover how you can leave more than you take.

rules.rule: Myth is the spine, not the decoration.
rules.why: The gala's motifs — the Sun, the star, the veil, the net, the open hand — may carry section transitions and the story chapters. Programme facts (dates, titles, tracks) stay literal and unadorned. Never write a schedule in metaphor.
rules.do: Section transition: 'When they lost sight of earth, they read the heavens.' → WHY NOW?
rules.dont: 'Set sail on Day 2 for a voyage through our think tanks…'

rules.rule: British English and the deck's proper casing.
rules.why: The deck writes organisation, programme, personalisation, civilisation, standardise. Named things keep their caps: MED READY, 11 FOR 11, BRAIN, SUN, Türkiye, Forbes Travel Guide Plus.

rules.rule: No exclamation marks. No superlatives. No urgency except a date.
rules.why: pear.no: nothing bounces. The deck never says world-class, unmissable, or exciting. The only permitted pressure is '25–27 November 2026'.
rules.dont: Don't miss the most exciting tourism event of the year!

microcopy.eyebrowStyle: 9–12px mono, uppercase, letterspaced, optional translucent chip — e.g. 'DAY 02 — 26 NOVEMBER', '11 FOR 11 · REGIONAL ACTION', 'THE GALA'.
microcopy.footerTagline: Think together. Learn together. Act together.
